title: One SDK for generation requests
summary:
This week made the path from picking a model to making a request—and understanding its cost—less mysterious.

The new @pollinations/sdk brings image, video, text, chat, audio, and model-list requests into one package for Node.js and browsers. It includes streaming, conversation and batch helpers, typed responses, retries, and timeouts. It replaces the old React package, but does not include its hooks. An OpenCode setup helper also reduced the configuration needed to use Pollinations models with agents.

SANA-Sprint gained an image backend, `flux` once again selects Flux Schnell, and `qwen-coder` moved to Qwen3-Coder. GLM-4.7 and MiniMax-M2.1 joined the reasoning lineup. Perplexity reasoning, Claude, Nova Micro, and Kimi received routing or naming updates, while text-generation validation learned to accept aliases from the shared model registry. Model names should require less guesswork than model names usually do.

Gemini gained code execution, Google Search, and caller-supplied URL context; chat responses can include generated image blocks such as plots. Follow-up work resolved structured-output tool conflicts. Plain-text `/text` responses now append source URLs when citations are returned, unsupported response formats produce errors instead of successful-looking fallback text, and Play renders video results in a video player.

Enter’s model table now groups text, image, and video models and shows full names. Pollen estimates use observed usage when available, backed by workload-based estimates, and a public endpoint exposes aggregated model usage for the last seven complete days. Key guidance, model selection, and authorization wording were clarified; the legacy auth page now points people to Enter for account and token management.
